issues.description: The blanket paging-constants implementation repeats two trait-owned `when_used_as_spec` mappings, causing the supported Verus to reject `lock-protocol` before verification.
issues.rationale: The selected merge already declares `when_used_as_spec` on `PagingConstsTrait::BASE_PAGE_SIZE` and `NR_LEVELS`, but repeats each mapping on `impl<C: PageTableConfig> PagingConstsTrait for C`. With exact supported Verus 8ae07c, the first attribute aborts on unresolved `BASE_PAGE_SIZE_SPEC`; removing only that attribute exposes the independent unresolved `NR_LEVELS_SPEC` failure. Independent controlled variants show each attribute fails by itself and deleting only both attributes, while retaining all implementation postconditions and the duplicated trait equality, gives 304 verified and 0 errors. Repair commit 40b97821 removes the two obsolete implementation mappings and also verifies 304/0.
issues.source_evidence:
after/lock-protocol/src/mm/page_table/mod.rs
130:     #[verifier::when_used_as_spec(BASE_PAGE_SIZE_SPEC)]
131:     fn BASE_PAGE_SIZE() -> (res: usize)
132:         ensures
133:             res == Self::BASE_PAGE_SIZE_SPEC(),
...
142:     #[verifier::when_used_as_spec(NR_LEVELS_SPEC)]
143:     fn NR_LEVELS() -> (res: PagingLevel)
144:         ensures
145:             res == Self::NR_LEVELS_SPEC(),

The trait already owns the same mappings at lines 279 and 294. Fixed Verus reports `cannot find function referred to in when_used_as_spec: lib::mm::page_table::BASE_PAGE_SIZE_SPEC`; after removing only that attribute it reports the corresponding `NR_LEVELS_SPEC` error. Attribute-only removal of both gives `304 verified, 0 errors`.
issues.verification: Reproduced with Verus 8ae07cceb1d1f0b17ca186faff4ba298eb6b33dd (0.2025.06.22.8ae07cc) and Rust 1.85.1-aarch64-apple-darwin. Exact problem: vstd_extra 228/0 and aster_common 253/0, then lock-protocol aborts on the first mapping. Each single-attribute variant fails on its remaining mapping. Removing both attributes only gives lock-protocol 304/0; the actual repair tree also gives 304/0.
